comply-in.span: Semantic search for meaning, keyword search for exact matches, used where each excels.
A clear recommendation based on domain, data type, and query patterns.
Hybrid search blends vector and inverted index, the standard pattern for balanced retrieval.
If your use case doesn't benefit from hybrid, I'll explain why.

sec-head.h2: What is Semantic Search? What is Keyword Search?

p: Semantic search uses vector embeddings to understand query intent and meaning, excelling at synonyms and conceptual matches. Keyword search matches exact terms against an inverted index, ideal for structured lookups and rare terms. Both are open-source (e.g., Elasticsearch, Pinecone), and the real decision hinges on whether your queries need meaning or precision.

sec-head.h2: Comparison: Semantic Search vs Keyword Search

td: Exact term and inverted index matching
Precise term lookup, structured queries, IDs
Requires embeddings model, vector DB, tuning
Typically 5–20ms for vector search (depends on index)
1–5ms for term search over inverted index
Rare terms, exact code snippets, out-of-vocabulary

p: Production search systems increasingly combine both: keyword search for exact high-precision results and semantic search for recall on ambiguous queries. Hybrid search (e.g., reciprocal rank fusion) is the standard architecture when neither approach alone satisfies.
